sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: Established on **October 31, 1920**, in Bombay, primarily to secure representation for Indian workers at the **International Labour Organization (ILO)**.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: The inaugural session was presided over by **Lala Lajpat Rai**, who emphasized the need for a centralized body to coordinate labor strikes and demands.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: The organization was heavily influenced by the **Russian Revolution** and the global rise of **Socialism/Communism**, leading to internal ideological friction between moderates and radicals.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The **1929 Nagpur Session** marked a critical turning point where the split occurred between the reformist leadership and the radical communist faction.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Dominated by moderate nationalists like N.M. Joshi and Lala Lajpat Rai.
Need for ILO representation and basic labor welfare.
Prelims: Focus on founding members and the 1920 date.
Entry of communists (Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed) and rise of militant trade unionism.
Influence of the Comintern and anti-imperialist sentiment.
Mains: Evolution of labor movement from reformist to revolutionary.

items.definition: Known as the 'Father of the Trade Union Movement in India'; he was the first General Secretary of AITUC and a moderate who prioritized labor welfare over political agitation.
The session presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru where the AITUC split; the radical faction formed the All India Red Trade Union Congress (RTUC) due to ideological differences.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Key Application 1**: Institutionalization of labor demands, moving from sporadic strikes to organized collective bargaining.
• **Key Application 2**: Integration of labor struggles with the broader Indian National Congress (INC) agenda, specifically during the Civil Disobedience Movement.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Internal ideological fragmentation (Moderates vs. Communists) and colonial repression (Trade Disputes Act, 1929).
• **Solutions**: Eventual reunification efforts in the late 1930s and the formation of the National Federation of Trade Unions (NFTU).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'L-N-J' (Lala, Nagpur, Joshi).
• **Decoded Meaning**: **L**ala Lajpat Rai (First President), **N**agpur (1929 Split), **J**oshi (N.M. Joshi, First General Secretary).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the founding year (1920) with the year of the split (1929). Also, remember that AITUC was NOT the only union; the NFTU and later INTUC were distinct entities.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Proletarian Internationalism' to describe the ideological shift within AITUC during the late 1920s.

keyTakeaways: AITUC was the first national-level trade union federation in India.
The 1929 Nagpur session is the most critical event for understanding the ideological split in the Indian labor movement.
The movement transitioned from purely economic welfare demands to active participation in the anti-colonial political struggle.
